Subject: Request: extract scope + delivery format for SOC2 evidence

Hi Rishi / Kimberly / Grace,

Thanks again for taking this. NovaHealth's SOC 2 auditor has asked for a short, concrete deliverable list for audit-log/admin-action evidence. Two asks up front:

1) Confirmation of what fields are emitted for admin/admin-like events (user id, service, action, resource id, source ip, timestamp with TZ, request id, before/after payload pointers).
2) Export delivery options and chain-of-custody details (signed manifest, checksums, encryption at rest/in-transit, S3 presigned vs SFTP).

Goal: provide the auditor a single package they can ingest and validate. We don't need a full snapshot now — a small sample + manifest and the export procedure will suffice for the pre-audit questionnaire.

Timing: auditor wants a sample by EOD Thursday (2028-08-24). Is that realistic?

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Request: extract scope + delivery format for SOC2 evidence

Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. We can do this. High-level answers first, then a short checklist we can send to the auditor.

What we log (out-of-the-box for operator/admin events):
- timestamp (RFC3339 with timezone)
- operator_id (email or service principal)
- action_type (create/update/delete/assign/role_change/privileged_access)
- resource_type and resource_id (model_id, deployment_id, route)
- request_id (UUID) and parent_request_id when available
- source_ip and geo (if resolvable)
- proto/agent/user_agent
- before/after diffs (for sensitive config changes we store diffs with redaction markers)
- outcome/status and error_code

Retention & snapshots:
- Hosted: 13 months default, can be extended for Dedicated/Private customers per contract.
- We retain immutable snapshots for sampling (signed manifests) for 90 days by default and can produce ad-hoc 1:1 snapshots for audits.

Export options we support:
- S3 put (server-side encrypted) with a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums). We provide presigned PUT links for secure transfer.
- SFTP push to customer endpoint (mutual TLS) — typically for very large bundles.
- HTTPS pull: temporary signed URLs to a tarball + manifest (expires configurable).

Chain-of-custody / attestation:
- Each export includes: manifest.json (fields, checksum list, start/end timestamps, exporter identity), manifest signature (our KMS-signed attestation), and a human-readable export statement.
- We provide an HMAC over the manifest + S3 ETag list and can provide a notarized block (if required under DPA).

Small sample delivery: we can produce a 7-day sample (anonymized) and a signed manifest by Thu EOD. Attachments I will send: export-field-map.csv (field list) and signed-manifest-template.json.

Action items (for us):
- I will prepare the sample and manifest, and a one-page export procedure for the auditor.
- Kimberly: can you confirm redaction defaults for PII in diffs?

Rishi
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Request: extract scope + delivery format for SOC2 evidence

Rishi / Alex —

Forwarding quick notes from the redaction/data-protection playbook:

- Redaction: by default we mask PII in before/after diffs (email, phone, ssn-like patterns) at export time unless customer opts into verbatim export for a controlled scope. Masking replaces with <REDACTED:FIELD_TYPE>.
- Timestamps: we provide both original TZ-aware timestamps and normalized UTC timestamps in the manifest to avoid ambiguity for auditors.
- Timebox: we can produce a signed 7-day sample in 48 hours; larger snapshots (90 days) typically take 3–5 business days for packaging and notarization.
- Proofing: we include a small reconciled count file (line counts per table/log type) to help auditors verify completeness.

Alex — I suggest we give the auditor the 7-day sample + manifest now and offer a schedule for a 90-day attested snapshot if they need deeper evidence.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
